questions.question: Where does globset turn a glob such as `src/**/*.rs` into the regular expression that is actually matched against paths?
questions.notes: GlobBuilder.build parses the pattern into Tokens and stores Tokens::to_regex_with(&opts, &tokens) as the glob's regex (glob.rs 600-631, 626). to_regex_with emits (?-u), (?i) when case-insensitive, anchors with ^...$ and special-cases a lone `**` as `.*` (694-711); tokens_to_regex maps each token: escaped literals, `?` to `.` or `[^/]` and `*` to `.*` or `[^/]*` depending on literal_separator, RecursivePrefix to `(?:/?|.*/)`, RecursiveSuffix to `/.*`, RecursiveZeroOrMore to `(?:/|/.*/)`, plus classes and `{a,b}` alternates (713-783). Wrong but plausible: Parser.parse_star (only tokenizes `*` and `**`, writes no regex), GlobSet.new / MatchStrategy.new (choose literal/extension shortcuts, the regex is the fallback), new_regex (compiles an already built regex string with regex-automata), GitignoreBuilder.add_line (rewrites a .gitignore line into a glob, not a regex).

questions.question: When I pass `--max-columns 150`, long lines are not printed but replaced by an 'omitted long line' notice (or a cut-off preview with `--max-columns-preview`). Which function writes that?
questions.notes: write_exceeded_line covers both modes: with max_columns_preview it keeps the first max_columns graphemes, writes them with colored matches and appends ' [... omitted end of long line]' or ' [... N more matches]' (standard.rs 1297-1328); otherwise it writes '[Omitted long context line]', '[Omitted long matching line]' or '[Omitted long line with N matches]' (1329-1351). exceeds_max_columns is only the byte-length test that write_line, write_colored_line and the multi-line sinks (1054, 1100, 1138) run before calling it. HiArgs.printer_standard passes --max-columns and --max-columns-preview to the builder (hiargs.rs 619-620). Wrong but plausible: exceeds_max_columns (the check only), StandardBuilder.max_columns (setter), the MaxColumns flag in core/flags/defs.rs (docs and parsing).

questions.question: If I mistype a flag, e.g. `rg --hiden foo`, the error lists similar flags that do exist. Which function picks those similar flag names?
questions.notes: Parser.parse bails with 'unrecognized flag --NAME' and appends suggest(&name) (parse.rs 265-270). suggest formats 'similar flags that are available: --a, --b' (404-415); find_similar_names compares the 3-gram bag of the unknown name with every long name, negated name and alias in FLAGS and keeps those with jaccard_index >= 0.4 (418-448). Wrong but plausible: suggest_pcre2 / suggest_multiline / suggest_other_engine / suggest_text in core/flags/hiargs.rs (1422-1480; they add a hint to use -P, -U or -a after a regex build error, not flag names), Parser.find_long / FlagMap.find (exact lookup only).

questions.question: In the parallel directory walker, which function lets a thread that has run out of directories steal queued work from another thread?
questions.notes: Each worker owns a Stack: a crossbeam LIFO deque (depth-first per thread) plus the Stealers of all threads (walk.rs 1648-1656, 1662-1689). Stack.pop takes from the local deque and falls back to steal() (1697-1699); steal tries the other stealers from index+1 onward, wraps around, skips itself and uses steal_batch_and_pop (1702-1714). Worker.recv is just stack.pop() (2015-2017). Wrong but plausible: Worker.get_work (quit/idle bookkeeping around recv, sleeps 1 ms when nothing is found), Stack.new_for_each_thread (round-robin initial distribution), WalkParallel.visit (creates stacks and spawns workers).

questions.question: Once the regex reports a match at some byte offset inside the search buffer, which function widens that offset to the start and end of the whole line that gets reported?
questions.notes: locate searches backwards (rfind_byte) for the previous line terminator and forwards (find_byte) for the next one and returns Match(line_start, line_end), the terminator included (lines.rs 134-147; #[inline(always)] at 134). It is called by Core.find_by_line_fast for Confirmed and Candidate offsets (core.rs 492-510) and by the multi-line searcher (glue.rs 222, 270). Wrong but plausible: LineStep / next_impl (iterate lines forward from a position), preceding / preceding_by_pos (find where before-context starts), without_terminator, the printer's trim_line_terminator.

questions.question: .gitignore dosyasindaki tek bir satir (basinda ! olan, / ile biten, icinde / gecmeyen gibi) nerede glob desenine cevriliyor?
questions.notes: Turkish without Turkish letters ('.gitignore dosyasındaki tek bir satır (başında ! olan, / ile biten, içinde / geçmeyen gibi) nerede glob desenine çevriliyor'). add_line skips '#' comments and blank lines, trims trailing spaces unless escaped, handles '\!' and '\#', marks '!' as a whitelist, a leading '/' as anchored and a trailing '/' as directory-only, prefixes '**/' when the line has no '/', appends '/*' to a trailing '/**', then builds the glob with literal_separator and backslash_escape (gitignore.rs 470-543). add reads a file line by line, strips a UTF-8 BOM and calls add_line (408-437). Wrong but plausible: OverrideBuilder.add (the -g/--glob path; it reuses add_line, but Override.matched inverts '!'), Tokens.to_regex_with in globset (glob to regex, one step later), Gitignore.matched_stripped (matching, where the last matching line wins).

questions.question: `--max-filesize 2M` gibi bir değerdeki `K`/`M`/`G` sonekini bayt sayısına çeviren fonksiyon hangisi?
questions.notes: parse_human_readable_size splits the leading ASCII digits from the suffix, returns the number as bytes when there is no suffix and multiplies by 1<<10, 1<<20, 1<<30 for K/M/G with checked_mul, returning ParseSizeError for a bad format, a bad integer or overflow (human.rs 79-100). The flag code reaches it through convert::human_readable_u64 (defs.rs 7602-7604; items of the inline `mod convert`), e.g. from MaxFilesize.update (4036-4040); --dfa-size-limit and --regex-size-limit use the same converter via human_readable_usize. Wrong but plausible: skip_filesize (applies the limit while walking), MaxFilesize.doc_long (only documents the suffixes), ParseSizeError (the error type).

questions.question: `rg -t rust` yazınca `rust` türünün `*.rs` dosyalarına karşılık geldiği yerleşik dosya türü listesi nerede tanımlı?
questions.notes: DEFAULT_TYPES is a #[rustfmt::skip] const slice of (names, globs) pairs, e.g. (&["rust"], &["*.rs"]) at line 246 and (&["py", "python"], ...) at 221 (default_types.rs 11-346). Given by lines and without a symbol because it is a `const` item (range starts at the #[rustfmt::skip] attribute). TypesBuilder.add_defaults adds every pair with add(name, glob) (types.rs 486-496); the core types() helper calls it before applying --type-add / --type-clear / -t / -T (hiargs.rs 1186-1206). Wrong but plausible: Types.matched (applies the selected types to a path), the --type-list printer types() in core/main.rs (329-348), TypesBuilder.add_def (parses a --type-add definition).

questions.question: When ripgrep has many globs at once (several `-g '*.rs' -g '*.toml' -g Makefile`, or all lines of a big .gitignore), how does it avoid running one regex per glob for every path it checks?
questions.notes: MatchStrategy.new classifies each glob as basename literal, full literal, extension ('*.rs'), prefix, suffix, required extension, basename regex or plain regex (glob.rs 53-71). GlobSet.new buckets them: literals and basenames into hash-map LiteralStrategy, extensions into ExtensionStrategy (a map keyed by the extension), prefixes and suffixes into Aho-Corasick matchers, and only the leftovers into one combined regex set built with MatchKind::All (lib.rs 461-564, 1052-1079). Matching dispatches per bucket in GlobSetMatchStrategy.is_match / matches_into. Wrong but plausible: Tokens.to_regex_with (builds the single-glob regex that GlobSet mostly avoids running), RegexSetStrategy alone (the fallback bucket), Gitignore.matched_stripped / Types.matched (consumers of a GlobSet).

questions.question: How does ripgrep notice that a file is binary (a NUL byte) while searching it, and where does it stop reading such a file?
questions.notes: Buffered reader path: LineBuffer.fill scans every newly read chunk; with BinaryDetection::Quit it cuts the buffer at the first NUL, records binary_byte_offset and behaves as EOF, with Convert it replaces NULs by the line terminator via replace_bytes (line_buffer.rs 434-462); ReadByLine.fill reports the offset to the sink and stops (glue.rs 58-93). Memory-map/slice path: Core.detect_binary looks for the byte in the first DEFAULT_BUFFER_CAPACITY (64 KB, SliceByLine.run 117-131) and again in every matched or context range (core.rs 215-238, called at 527-622). The policy comes from BinaryDetection.from_low_args: quit on NUL for files found by the walk, convert for paths named on the command line, none with -a/--null-data (hiargs.rs 1159-1175), selected per haystack in SearchWorker.search (search.rs 249-257). Wrong but plausible: StandardImpl.write_binary_message (prints the notice afterwards), the BinaryDetection constructors in searcher/mod.rs (wrap the enum only), the --binary / --text flag docs in defs.rs.

questions.question: Instead of running the full regex on every line, how does ripgrep use a cheap literal search to find candidate lines and only then confirm them with the real regex?
questions.notes: RegexMatcherBuilder.build_many stores fast_line_regex = InnerLiterals::new(&chir, &regex).one_regex() (matcher.rs 69-78). InnerLiterals.new declines without a line terminator, when the meta regex is already accelerated (unless it has Unicode word boundaries) or for a plain alternation of literals, else runs the Extractor (literal.rs 54-92); one_regex compiles the extracted literals into one alternation regex (106-122). RegexMatcher.find_candidate_line reports LineMatchKind::Candidate from that regex, or Confirmed through shortest_match when there is none (matcher.rs 490-506), and Core.find_by_line_fast expands the offset to its line with lines::locate and re-checks Candidate lines with is_match (core.rs 475-519; used when is_line_by_line_fast holds). Wrong but plausible: the regex engine's own prefilters (regex-automata / memchr, not in this repo), Core.match_by_line_slow (the line-at-a-time path without this trick), Extractor internals alone (only produce the literal set).

questions.question: When does ripgrep read a file through a memory map instead of its normal read buffer?
questions.notes: The decision is the `let mmap_choice = {...}` block inside HiArgs.from_low_args (hiargs.rs 222-249, given by lines because from_low_args spans 113-322): with the default --mmap auto it uses MmapChoice::auto() only when at most 10 paths were given and all are files, else never; --mmap forces auto, --no-mmap never. HiArgs.searcher passes it to SearcherBuilder.memory_map (726). Searcher.search_file_maybe_path asks MmapChoice.open and searches the map as a slice, else falls back to the multiline heap buffer or the incremental reader (mod.rs 678-714); open returns None when disabled and on macOS, maps the file, advises sequential access on Unix and logs and returns None on error (mmap.rs 65-115). stdin, --pre and -z inputs always go through search_reader (search.rs 258-266). Wrong but plausible: MmapChoice.auto (the unsafe constructor only), the --mmap flag docs in defs.rs, Searcher.search_slice (searches the map once it exists).

questions.question: Bir dosya hem `.ignore` hem `.gitignore` içinde farklı kurallarla geçiyorsa hangisi kazanır? Bu öncelik sırası nerede belirleniyor?
questions.notes: matched_ignore walks this directory and its parents, keeping the first (closest) match of each kind, and combines them as custom ignore files (.rgignore) > .ignore > .gitignore > .git/info/exclude > global gitignore > explicit --ignore-file (dir.rs 709-714); git-based files only count inside a git (or jj) repository unless require_git is off (590-592, 609-623). Ignore.matched puts -g overrides first, then the ignore files, then -t/-T types; an ignore verdict returns immediately and a whitelist is kept only if nothing later ignores (530-574). The per-directory matchers are built in add_child_path_with_found_ignore_files (.ignore, .gitignore, info/exclude; 389-470) and HiArgs.walk_builder registers .rgignore (hiargs.rs 904-906). Wrong but plausible: Gitignore.matched_stripped (precedence between lines of one file, last match wins), GitignoreBuilder.add_line (parsing), should_skip_entry (only logs and applies the verdict).

questions.question: --smart-case acikken desende buyuk harf yoksa arama buyuk/kucuk harfe duyarsiz yapiliyor; bu karar nerede veriliyor?
questions.notes: Turkish without Turkish letters ('--smart-case açıkken desende büyük harf yoksa arama büyük/küçük harfe duyarsız yapılıyor; bu karar nerede veriliyor'). Default engine: ConfiguredHIR.new parses the joined pattern to an AST, runs AstAnalysis::from_ast and passes config.is_case_insensitive(&analysis) to the HIR translator (config.rs 198-201); is_case_insensitive is true for -i and, under smart case, only when the pattern has a literal and no uppercase literal (84-92); AstAnalysis sets any_literal / any_uppercase from literals and class items, so \pL does not count (ast.rs 56-137). PCRE2 (-P) has its own check: build_many turns on caseless when has_uppercase_literal finds no uppercase char outside backslash escapes (pcre2/src/matcher.rs 64-66, 422-432). HiArgs.matcher_rust / matcher_pcre2 only forward CaseMode::Smart (hiargs.rs 471, 419). Wrong but plausible: RegexMatcherBuilder.case_smart (setter), the SmartCase flag in defs.rs, Config.is_fixed_strings (only declines the literal fast path under smart case).

questions.question: When ripgrep runs with several threads, how does a file found by the directory walker end up being searched and its matching lines printed?
questions.notes: search_parallel builds one SearchWorker and passes WalkParallel.run a closure factory; each walker thread clones the worker, turns every entry into a Haystack with build_from_result (files only), clears its printer buffer, calls searcher.search(&haystack) and prints the buffer through the BufferWriter so output from different files never interleaves (main.rs 175-218). SearchWorker.search sets binary detection and picks stdin / preprocessor / decompression / plain path (search.rs 245-267); the free search_path makes the printer's sink and calls Searcher.search_path (380-412), which opens the file, and search_file_maybe_path chooses memory map, multiline heap buffer or the incremental reader (mod.rs 643-714). The line loop (ReadByLine / SliceByLine -> Core.match_by_line) hands each match to the sink, and StandardSink.matched counts it, records match ranges, applies --replace and writes the line through StandardImpl (standard.rs 766-791). Wrong but plausible: search (the single-threaded twin, main.rs 107-151), Worker.run_one in the ignore crate (walks directories but searches nothing), Searcher.search_reader alone.

questions.question: --replace '$1' verdigimde eslesen satirdaki metin nasil degistiriliyor, $1 yakalama grubunun degerine nerede donusuyor?
questions.notes: Turkish without Turkish letters ('--replace '$1' verdiğimde eşleşen satırdaki metin nasıl değiştiriliyor, $1 yakalama grubunun değerine nerede dönüşüyor'). HiArgs.printer_standard passes --replace to StandardBuilder.replacement (hiargs.rs 626). For every match StandardSink.matched calls self.replace (standard.rs 778), which runs Replacer.replace_all when a replacement is set (741-760). replace_all strips the line terminator, then replace_with_captures_in_context walks captures_iter_at and for each match caps.interpolate(...) appends the expanded replacement, recording its span for coloring (util.rs 51-109, 557-589). Captures.interpolate resolves group indices against the haystack (lib.rs 440-460); interpolate scans for '$', turns '$$' into '$', parses $N / $name / ${name} with find_cap_ref and appends the group text (interpolate.rs 13-56, 96-134). Wrong but plausible: Part.interpolate_to / Interpolator in printer/src/hyperlink/mod.rs (the --hyperlink-format {path}/{line} variables), Matcher.replace in matcher/src/lib.rs (901-919; closure-based, not used by the printer), JSONSink.replace (the --json twin).

questions.question: How do the arguments I type on the command line and the ones in the file named by `RIPGREP_CONFIG_PATH` get merged into the final settings that `main` uses, and which side wins on a conflict?
questions.notes: main calls run(flags::parse()) (main.rs 43-44). parse = parse_low followed by HiArgs::from_low_args (parse.rs 49-54). parse_low parses the CLI once (logging, -h/-V, --no-config), then config::args reads RIPGREP_CONFIG_PATH, appends the real CLI arguments after the config arguments and re-parses everything into a fresh LowArgs, so CLI flags come later and override the config file (parse.rs 64-113). config::args returns nothing when the variable is unset or empty and reports an unreadable file (config.rs 16-53); parse_reader keeps one argument per non-empty line that does not start with '#' (84-108). HiArgs.from_low_args then derives threads, color, line numbers, mmap, binary detection and the matchers' inputs (hiargs.rs 113-322). Wrong but plausible: Parser.parse alone (one pass over one argument list), LowArgs in lowargs.rs (plain field struct), the per-flag Flag.update methods in defs.rs.

questions.question: Where is the regex engine itself implemented, the NFA / lazy DFA code that scans a file's bytes for my pattern?
questions.notes: The engines live in the regex-automata crate (meta::Regex choosing among its NFA, one-pass DFA, full DFA and lazy/hybrid DFA) on top of regex-syntax, and with -P in the pcre2 crate / libpcre2. ripgrep only configures and calls them: ConfiguredHIR.to_regex sets nfa_size_limit, onepass and DFA limits and hybrid_cache_capacity (--dfa-size-limit) and builds the meta Regex from the HIR (config.rs 242-260); RegexMatcherBuilder.build_many calls it (matcher.rs 65) and RegexMatcher.find_at runs self.regex.find on an Input span (413-421). Correct behaviour: say the engine is not in the repo and cite the pointer. Wrong but plausible: InnerLiterals / fast_line_regex (ripgrep's own literal prefilter, not the engine), Core.find_by_line_fast (the line loop), globset's new_regex (also only builds a regex-automata Regex).

questions.question: UTF-16 ile kaydedilmiş bir dosyayı ararken baytları UTF-8'e çeviren kod (decoder) nerede yazılmış?
questions.notes: Transcoding is done by the encoding_rs_io crate (DecodeReaderBytes) on top of encoding_rs, not in this repo. SearcherBuilder.build configures a DecodeReaderBytesBuilder with the -E encoding, utf8_passthru, BOM stripping and sniffing (mod.rs 315-337), and Searcher.search_reader wraps every reader with build_with_buffer before the line search (740-744). For memory-mapped slices, search_slice falls back to search_reader when slice_needs_transcoding sees -E or a UTF-8/UTF-16 BOM (769-795, 824-827, 1036-1044). HiArgs.searcher maps -E / --no-encoding onto the builder (hiargs.rs 738-746). Correct behaviour: say the decoder is not in the repo and cite the pointer. Wrong but plausible: slice_has_bom (only detects the BOM), Encoding.new (label lookup in encoding_rs), LineBuffer.fill (reads already-decoded bytes).

questions.question: -z ile .gz dosyalarini ararken gzip acma (decompress) algoritmasi hangi dosyada?
questions.notes: Turkish without Turkish letters ('-z ile .gz dosyalarını ararken gzip açma algoritması hangi dosyada'). ripgrep has no decompressor: default_decompression_commands maps *.gz / *.tgz to 'gzip -d -c' and likewise bzip2, xz, lz4, lzma, brotli, zstd and uncompress (decompress.rs 490-532); DecompressionReaderBuilder.build spawns the matching command on the path through CommandReaderBuilder and falls back to reading the raw file when it cannot start (221-244); SearchWorker.search_decompress feeds that reader to the searcher (search.rs 329-339). The algorithms run in the external gzip / xz / ... programs. Correct behaviour: say it is not in the repo and cite the pointer. Wrong but plausible: DecompressionReader / CommandReader (only pipe the child's stdout), resolve_binary (finds the program on PATH on Windows), SearchWorker.search_preprocessor (the --pre external command, a different path).
